title_en: Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon on AI: Implementation, Accountability, and Jo
title_zh: Goldman Sachs 董事长兼 CEO David Solomon 谈 AI：落地、问责与创造就业
subtitle_zh: David Solomon 论 AI 需有护栏与问责，及其对就业与小企业的影响
description: Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon on AI: Implementation, Accountability, and Jo

turns.en: How do we get the societal benefits of AI while guarding against its risks? In a recent op-ed, today's guest argues that winning in the AI era is not a choice between innovation and safety.
turns.zh: 如何在享受 AI 带来的社会收益的同时，防范它的风险？在最近一篇署名评论文章（op-ed）里，我们今天的嘉宾提出：在 AI 时代取胜，并不是要在创新和安全之间二选一。

turns.en: I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges. Joining me is David Solomon, Chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs. We'll talk about how AI can be advanced with discipline, what AI means for jobs, how businesses are using it, and who should set the rules.
turns.zh: 我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs《Exchanges》。今天和我一起的是 Goldman Sachs 董事长兼 CEO David Solomon。我们会聊聊如何有章法地推进 AI，AI 对就业意味着什么，企业正在怎么用它，以及规则该由谁来定。

turns.en: We'll also discuss the firm's new commitment to help small businesses adopt AI. David, thanks for joining us. Thank you. Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 我们还会谈公司新近宣布的一项承诺——帮助小企业采用 AI。David，感谢你来参加节目。——谢谢。谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: It's great to have you here in the studio. You and I usually have a conversation at the start of the year to talk about what lies ahead, but we're sitting down today again to focus on the topic that seems to be on everyone's mind, AI.
turns.zh: 很高兴你来到演播室。你和我通常会在年初聊一次，谈谈未来会怎样，但今天我们再次坐下来，聚焦那个似乎人人都在关心的话题——AI。

turns.en: So in your op-ed that was published last Friday, you argued that the AI debate is too focused on a choice between moving fast without guardrails or heavy-handed restrictions that could slow progress.
turns.zh: 在你上周五发表的那篇署名评论里，你提出：如今关于 AI 的争论，太纠结于要么狂奔、没有护栏，要么就用重手监管、可能拖慢进步——这二者只能选其一。

turns.en: So what's that debate missing? Well, I think the debate's missing nuance. Most things that are complex and important aren't so binary. And so the narrative that's developed that if for some reason we don't let the innovation be unleashed and run at whatever speed with no guardrails, no protections, no risk and controls, we somehow inhibit our competitive position.
turns.zh: 那么这场争论到底缺了什么？我想，争论缺的是细腻的分辨。复杂而重要的事情，大多不是非此即彼那么二元的。如今形成的那种叙事是说：如果因为某种原因，我们不把创新彻底释放、让它不顾一切地全速狂奔——没有护栏、没有保护、没有风险管控——那我们就会以某种方式削弱自己的竞争地位。

turns.en: So therefore, the choice is to regulate, slow down, and stop and weaken our competitive position. I just don't think it's a binary choice. I think it's a much more nuanced discussion.
turns.zh: 所以，选择就变成了：要么去监管、放慢脚步、停下来，从而削弱我们的竞争地位。我觉得这根本不是一个二选一的问题，这是一次远比这更细腻、更需要斟酌的讨论。

turns.en: I think we absolutely can spur great innovation with this technology, but we have to have rules of the road. There have to be guardrails. There has to ultimately be a structure of accountability around the deployment of this technology into society in a way where we can really hold people accountable for the end result and what happens.
turns.zh: 我认为我们完全能够借助这项技术催生出伟大的创新，但我们得有交通规则，得有护栏，最终还得有一套关于把这项技术部署进社会的问责结构——让我们能真正就最终结果、就发生的事情，让人承担责任。

turns.en: And I think we can do that. I don't think it's different with this technology versus others, but it requires a more thoughtful nuanced discussion than some of this binary, let it run or let's regulate a control, let's stop it, slow it down.
turns.zh: 我觉得我们做得到。我认为这项技术和其他技术相比并没有本质不同，但它需要比那些'要么放任自流、要么上监管严控、要么干脆停下来慢下来'的二元论更缜密、更细腻的讨论。

turns.en: You see the responsibility for control. First sits with governments, second with the companies that are building these AI models, and third with the businesses using them.
turns.zh: 你把管控的责任这样排序：第一是政府，第二是构建这些 AI 模型的公司，第三是使用它们的企业。

turns.en: And it's really that third area that is getting less attention. Why are companies deploying AI as important as the other two layers of responsibility?
turns.zh: 而真正少受关注的恰恰是这第三块。为什么部署 AI 的企业，和另外两层责任同等重要？

turns.en: What I tried to do in the op-ed is I was trying to create a simple framework to enhance the conversation. And so I think very simply, and this is a simple summary of what's in the op-ed, government needs to play a role and set some rules of the road.
turns.zh: 我在文章里想做的，是搭建一个简单的框架来推动这场对话。很简单地说——这是文章内容的粗略概括——政府需要发挥作用，制定一些交通规则。

turns.en: The people that are developing these models and the infrastructure that allow the technology to exist and ultimately to be deployed in the economy have to take responsibility for what they're building and that it works and that it doesn't do harm.
turns.zh: 那些开发模型、搭建基础设施，让这项技术得以存在并最终部署到经济中去的人，必须为他们所构建的东西负责——它得真的管用，不能造成伤害。

turns.en: And then the companies that take those products and embed them and their enterprises and their service have to be responsible for the way they're deployed and the impact that they have.
turns.zh: 然后，把这些产品嵌入自家企业和服务里的那些公司，必须为它们的部署方式和所产生的影响负责。

turns.en: And the third's not getting as much attention, but it's equally important. Goldman Sachs has been using AI-type models for trading platforms for almost 20 years, but there's human accountability attached to every one of those platforms.
turns.zh: 第三块没得到同样多的关注，但它同样重要。Goldman Sachs 在交易平台上的 AI 类模型几乎已经用了 20 年，但每一个这样的平台背后都挂着人的问责。

turns.en: I could never imagine someone a Goldman Sachs enemy, the trading platform went off and did something awful on its own. We couldn't stop it. We wouldn't deploy it if we didn't feel that we had the control to manage it appropriately and that there was a human being that was ultimately accountable for anything that goes wrong.
turns.zh: 我绝难想象，Goldman Sachs 的某个交易平台会自己跑出去做出什么糟糕的事、我们还拦不住它。如果我们没有把握去妥善管控它，如果没有一个人最终为任何差错承担责任，我们是不会部署它的。

turns.en: That's just one example of what needs to happen, but the enterprises have to be responsible for what they deploy into their businesses. The financial services sector uses risk management principles and tools that could help developers and employers.
turns.zh: 这只是需要做到的一件事的一个例子，企业必须为它们在自己业务里部署的东西负责。金融行业所用的风险管理原则和工具，能够帮助开发者和雇主。

turns.en: Tell us more about that. What approach do you think makes the most sense here? There's been some talk of replicating certain practices that we've seen develop over time with financial services regulation, but these are different things.
turns.zh: 多给我们讲讲这个。你觉得这里哪种做法最合理？外界一直在讨论，能否复制金融行业监管多年来形成的一些做法，但这两者其实是不同的东西。

turns.en: I do think though there's a lot that can be learned from the experience that large financial institutions have had, particularly around risk management.
turns.zh: 不过我确实认为，大型金融机构在风险管理方面积累的经验，有很多值得学习的地方。

turns.en: Financial institutions, particularly the large financial institutions have developed great risk and control practices, great audit practices, great testing practices over a long period of time, given some of the experiences 20 years ago in the financial crisis, these institutions have learned how to really build up the right infrastructure to test, control, and earn trust.
turns.zh: 金融机构，尤其是大型金融机构，在很长的时间里发展出了出色的风险与管控实践、出色的审计实践、出色的测试实践——这得益于大约 20 年前金融危机里的那些经历。这些机构已经学会了如何搭建起恰当的测试、管控和赢得信任的基础设施。

turns.en: Ultimately, that needs to happen here. There are businesses that are going to deploy this technology into their enterprise that have great experience in doing those kinds of things, and there are others that need to learn that it's a new muscle group.
turns.zh: 说到底，这里也得走这条路。有些企业会在自家业务里部署这项技术，它们在这一类事情上有很丰富的经验；也有些企业需要明白，这是一块全新的肌肉。

turns.en: They haven't had to have risk and control processes of the same level that are going to be necessary for this technology, and they're going to have to figure that out.
turns.zh: 它们过去从不需要与这项技术所要求的同等水平的风险与管控流程，接下来它们得把这一课补上。

turns.en: If we put this all together, David, what does winning in the AI era look like from a safety and innovation perspective? AI is a tremendous technology that I think is going to have enormous societal benefits, but with anything else that's new and is creating change, there are going to be risk issues, there are going to be speed bumps, and it's our responsibility as a society to figure out how to implement that and put the proper controls into place.
turns.zh: 如果把这些都串起来，David，从安全和创新的角度看，在 AI 时代取胜是什么样子？AI 是一项了不起的技术，我相信它会带来巨大的社会效益；但和其他一切新生事物、一切正在制造变化的东西一样，一定会有风险问题、会有减速带，而作为社会，我们的责任是搞清楚如何落实它、把恰当的管控措施到位。

turns.en: If we do that, we'll reap the benefits, and while at times things will go wrong or there will be friction, we will generally control them. By the way, that's true with almost any technology that accelerates growth, productivity, economic activity.
turns.zh: 如果我们做到了，就会收获它的益处；虽然有时会有差错、会有摩擦，但我们总体上能把它控制住。顺带一提，几乎所有能加速增长、生产力和经济活动的技术都是如此。

turns.en: We can do that successfully. Winning, if you want to use that expression, is that we get the benefits of what this technology can do in terms of solving problems and science and wellness and health, drug discovery, disease.
turns.zh: 我们完全能把它做成功。要说'取胜'——如果你要用这个词的话——那就是我们收获这项技术能带来的种种好处：解决科学、健康、福祉、药物研发、疾病等方面的问题。

turns.en: There are all sorts of things that you can think about where we can reap enormous benefits. Winning is that we get those benefits, but we have built a system where there's trust and there's a belief that we can manage the risks associated with the technology as it's deployed, and I think we can accomplish that.
turns.zh: 你能想到的方方面面，我们都能从中获得巨大的裨益。所谓取胜，就是我们既拿到了这些好处，又建立起了一个有信任的体系——让人们相信，随着技术被部署，我们有能力管控它的风险。我认为我们做得到。

turns.en: I'm optimistic we can accomplish that. I'm very optimistic about the potential for the technology and what it can achieve. Also optimistic in terms of the implications for jobs, which has obviously been very much in focus, you've described two camps among business leaders, those expecting a job apocalypse, and those expecting a great leap forward.
turns.zh: 我对做到这点是乐观的。我对这项技术的潜力、对它所能实现的东西非常乐观。对就业层面的影响我也同样乐观，这一点显然一直备受关注——你描述过商界领袖中的两派：一派预期会出现就业末日，另一派预期会迎来一次大跃升。

turns.en: Where do you lean and what needs to happen for it to play out? I'm more in the second camp than the first camp with some caveats. Whenever you create new technology, new technology disrupts and automates, and this technology is going to disrupt and automate, and there's just no question that we're going to see that.
turns.zh: 你更倾向于哪一边？要让它往好的方向发展，需要发生什么？我更偏向第二派而不是第一派，但有一些前提。每当出现新技术，新技术都会带来颠覆、都会自动化，这项技术也会颠覆、会自动化，毫无疑问我们终将看到这一点。

turns.en: The question is at what pace, and the question also that doesn't get enough attention is, because of this technology, what new businesses spring up, what new jobs are created?
turns.zh: 问题在于以什么样的速度；还有一个关注不够的问题是：正因为有了这项技术，会冒出哪些新企业、创造出哪些新工作？

turns.en: Remember, we have a very, very dynamic economy in the US. We create and destroy on average 30 million jobs every year. We generally create a million more than we destroy on average.
turns.zh: 记住，我们美国的经济非常、非常有活力。我们平均每年创造又消灭 3000 万个工作岗位。总体上，我们平均每年创造的比消灭的多出 100 万个。

turns.en: A lot of those jobs come from small businesses. By the way, there's a great opportunity for small businesses to use this technology to accelerate their ability to grow, bring the cost down in the context of infrastructure they need to be successful.
turns.zh: 很多这样的工作是由小企业创造的。顺带一提，小企业这里有一个很好的机会：用这项技术来加快自身增长、把成本降下来，搭建起它们成功所需要的基础设施。

turns.en: So broadly speaking, while there'll be disruption, I think there'll also be counterbalances to that. Now, here's a question that I think we've got to watch.
turns.zh: 所以总体而言，尽管会有颠覆，我认为也会有与之相抗衡的对冲力量。这里有一个我觉得我们必须留意的地方。

turns.en: If the pace of this change is happening quickly, the bridge between the benefits and the jobs that are created and jobs that are being automated could be quicker.
turns.zh: 如果这场变化来得太快，那么收益、被创造出来的工作与被自动化掉的工作之间的这座'桥'，衔接可能会过于仓促。

turns.en: We might need some policy actions to soften that disruption. I also think you have to realize that a lot of what this technology does is it makes smart people more productive.
turns.zh: 我们可能需要一些政策举措来缓冲这场冲击。我还觉得，你必须认识到，这项技术所做的很多事情，是让聪明人更有生产力。

turns.en: So when people talk about why college jobs, just because the technology makes them more productive, it doesn't mean the job goes away, it means that the smart people can do more productive things while getting the benefit of the technology and their workflows.
turns.zh: 所以当人们谈到知识型工作时——仅仅因为技术让他们更有生产力，并不意味着工作会消失；它意味着聪明的人可以借助技术、融入自己的工作流，去做更有生产力的事。

turns.en: So there's going to be a lot of automation, a lot of workflow changes and the things that people do. But by the way, you can look back and notice that this has been going on for decades and decades and this is the next phase of that evolution.
turns.zh: 所以会有大量的自动化，大量的工作流和人们工作内容发生变化。但顺带一提，你可以回头看看，会发现这种演变已经持续了几十年又几十年，而这只是它的下一个阶段。

turns.en: I think about when I started, how I spent my time as a young analyst and what the productivity of our young analysts are today, we don't have less of them.
turns.zh: 我会想起我刚入行、作为一名年轻分析师时是怎么安排时间的，再看看我们今天的年轻分析师有多高的生产力——我们的分析师并没有变少。

turns.en: They just do different things and they're much more productive than they were 40 years ago. And so that's a good line. There are lots of jobs that have gone away because of technology and as we do that, we create new jobs in our economy.
turns.zh: 他们只是在做不同的事，而且比 40 年前的同行高效得多。所以这条参照很有意思。因为技术，有很多工作消失了；而我们在这样做的同时，也在经济里创造了新的工作。

turns.en: I'm confident and optimistic that will happen over the next decade or two. I think one of the things we have to watch carefully is in the short term, is there a little bit more disruption and does that require some policy actions or some steps to smooth that out?
turns.zh: 我相信并对未来一二十年这一切会发生感到乐观。我觉得我们必须格外留意的一点是：短期内，会不会有那么多一点更剧烈的颠覆，以至于需要一些政策举措或一些步骤去把它熨平？

turns.en: So what's your message or advice for analysts who might be worried that their job is going to disappear? I understand that people, when there's change, people are fearful, but my advice is want to embrace the technology, because the technology, if you're in a knowledge type job, the technology is going to be an important tool to embrace it, learn how to use it, learn how to make yourself more productive in that context.
turns.zh: 那么，对于一个担心自己工作会消失的分析师，你有什么话或者建议？我理解，当有变化发生时，人们会感到害怕。但我的建议是：你要去拥抱这项技术，因为如果你从事的是知识型工作，这项技术会是一件重要的工具——去拥抱它、学会用它、学会在这当中让自己更有生产力。

turns.en: But the world is always changing. The most successful people adapt and be prepared to adapt and figure out how your productivity can be enhanced in whatever job you're in.
turns.zh: 但世界一直在变。最成功的那些人，都是会适应的人。要准备好去适应，去想清楚无论你身处什么岗位，你的生产力都可以被提升。

turns.en: And that's something everybody should be doing all the time. If we bring this conversation to what we're doing here at Goldman Sachs, where is AI changing the work people do, including through AI agents, which have been incredibly in focus this year, and what surprised you most as we have adapted and integrated AI into our workflows so far?
turns.zh: 这是每个人时时刻刻都该做的事。如果我们把话题拉回到我们在 Goldman Sachs 正在做的事——AI 正在哪些地方改变人们的工作，包括通过 AI 智能体（AI agents），今年这一概念受到了极大关注——以及到目前为止，当我们把 AI 融入、整合进工作流的过程中，最让你意外的是什么？

turns.en: We're really focused, in the most simplistic way, we're focused on automation of processes and we're focused on enhancing client experience.
turns.zh: 我们真正专注的，说得最朴素一点，就是专注在两件事上：流程的自动化，以及提升客户体验。

turns.en: And so there are lots of ways we can get at that. We have always been very good at giving our very productive people who face clients technology tools and having them figure out how those technology tools enhance the way they serve clients.
turns.zh: 实现这一点有很多路径。我们向来擅长给那些直接面对客户的高产能员工提供技术工具，让他们自己琢磨出这些工具如何增强他们服务客户的方式。

turns.en: And we're on that journey now with this technology. I think the early signs of the benefits that the client experience is going to get are really quite encouraging.
turns.zh: 我们现在正带着这项技术走在这条路上。我觉得，客户体验即将获得的那些好处，初步的迹象已经相当令人鼓舞。

turns.en: And by the way, they also allow technology, allows an individual to see more clients have a bigger footprint. I think about what my client footprint was 40 years ago based on the tools that were available versus what it would be for somebody that was in a client role today.
turns.zh: 而且顺带一提，技术还让一个人能够服务更多客户、拥有更大的覆盖面。我会想，40 年前依据当时可用的工具，我的客户覆盖面有多大，而今天身处客户岗位的人又会是多少。

turns.en: And that's always enhanced and creates productivity. And that's a super exciting thing. I think the more complicated thing for all enterprises is how you redo operating processes and automate them in ways where you create real productivity gains and efficiency.
turns.zh: 这一直在增强、一直在创造生产力，是一件非常令人兴奋的事。我觉得对所有企业来说更复杂的那件事，是你如何重构运营流程、以创造价值与效率的方式去自动化它们。

turns.en: And then when you get that productivity and efficiency, what do you do with that? Are you just getting margin or operating leverage? Are you also creating capacity to invest in growth in your business in some place where you'd like more capacity to invest in growth?
turns.zh: 而当你拿到了这种生产力和效率，你拿它怎么办？你是只换来利润率、经营杠杆，还是也借此腾出能力，去投入到你希望有更多资源去扩张增长的地方？

turns.en: We see lots of opportunities to invest in growth in our business and we're trying to use efficiencies from automating processes to give ourselves more capability to drive investment and growth.
turns.zh: 我们在自己业务里看到很多可以投入增长的机会，我们正努力把流程自动化带来的效率，转化为我们推动投资与增长的更多能力。

turns.en: On that point, Goldman Sachs, of course, advises and finances companies building and using AI. Where is the firm having the biggest impact in this AI investment cycle that everyone is so focused on?
turns.zh: 就这一点而言，Goldman Sachs 当然在为那些构建和使用 AI 的公司提供咨询和融资。在这个所有人如此关注的 AI 投资周期里，公司在哪些方面影响最大？

turns.en: Well, the firm's an advisor. It's a financier. It also has extraordinary technology capabilities. I think we're deploying all those things to help governments and enterprises really think about how they can use this technology most effectively.
turns.zh: 我们是一家做顾问的公司，是做融资的公司，还拥有着非凡的技术能力。我想我们把这几样全用上，去帮助政府和企业真正思考如何最有效地运用这项技术。

turns.en: And so, certainly, we're giving a lot of advice to companies, to boards around how they can think about deploying this and what the benefits can be and how they should think about quantifying the economic benefit of the spend.
turns.zh: 所以，我们当然在给大量公司、给董事会提建议——它们该怎么考虑部署这项技术，好处会是什么，以及它们该怎么去量化这笔支出带来的经济效益。

turns.en: But in addition, there's an enormous amount of capital formations. It's necessary to build the infrastructure to drive this technology and through our capital solutions group and our very unique ability to act as an advisor, to have huge sourcing capability, but also have an asset management arm attached to the firm, we're in a very unique position or in the middle of a lot of the financing activity and playing a very
turns.zh: 但除此之外，还有极其庞大的资本形成——推动这项技术所需要的基础设施必须靠资本去建。通过我们的资本方案部门（capital solutions group），以及我们作为顾问那种独特的能力——我们有巨大的项目挖掘能力，同时公司旗下又连着一条资产管理线——我们处在很多融资活动的正中间，扮演着非常重要的角色。

turns.en: significant role. Let's switch gears to conclude and talk about smaller businesses, their role in the AI economy, and of course, the announcement that the firm made last week, Goldman has committed $500 million to launch the Small Business AI Institute with some of the leading AI labs.
turns.zh: ……扮演着非常重要的角色。我们换个话题来收尾，聊聊小企业、它们在 AI 经济里的角色，当然还有公司上周宣布的那件事：Goldman 承诺投入 5 亿美元，与一些领先的 AI 实验室共同发起'小企业 AI 学院'（Small Business AI Institute）。

turns.en: Why are small businesses so important to the AI economy here? Well, small businesses are important to our economy here, period. Small businesses by count are 99% of all the companies in the United States, but small businesses drive between 16 and 65% of the job creation in the United States every year.
turns.zh: 为什么小企业对这里的 AI 经济如此重要？因为小企业对我们这里的经济重要，句号。按数量算，小企业占美国全部公司的 99%，而小企业每年驱动着美国 16% 到 65% 的新增就业。

turns.en: Small businesses are a vitally important part of our economic ecosystem, a huge part of this service economy. Giving these businesses tools that allow entrepreneurs of small businesses to accelerate their growth, pursue their passions more aggressively.
turns.zh: 小企业是我们经济生态里至关重要的组成部分，是这个服务型经济的巨大部分。给这些企业提供工具，让小企业的创业者能更快增长、更放手地去追求他们的热爱——

turns.en: That's one of the things about entrepreneurs, they're picking businesses where they have passion. There's an expense to building a business, building a platform, setting it up.
turns.zh: 这就是创业者身上的一点：他们选择的是自己热爱的事业。创业、搭平台、把它立起来，是有成本的。

turns.en: That expense is going down with this technology, so that gives more entrepreneurs the opportunity to start businesses. It's a really positive thing, but they need help.
turns.zh: 而这项技术正在把这种成本降下来，于是给了更多创业者创业的机会。这是非常积极的事，但他们需要帮助。

turns.en: They need coaching. They need understanding. They need people that have more experience with these tools and the deployment of technology into an enterprise, even if it's a small enterprise.
turns.zh: 他们需要辅导，需要理解，需要那些对这些工具、对把技术部署进企业——哪怕是一家很小的企业——更有经验的人。

turns.en: The AI Institute, we made a $500 million commitment to really do a couple of things. It's a continuation of our broad 10,000 small business platform, where at this point over the last, I think, 17 years, we've had 20,000 companies, small businesses go through the program, this business education program, but now we're going to make to those businesses and new businesses AI training available so they can really test how AI can be used in
turns.zh: 'AI 学院'这件事，我们做出了 5 亿美元的承诺，主要想做到几件事。它是我们'万名小企业'（10,000 small business）平台的延续——过去，我想大概 17 年里，已经有 2 万家公司、小企业走过这个商业教育项目；而现在我们要让这些企业，也包括新企业，能够拿到 AI 培训，这样它们就能真正测试 AI 能怎么用在——

turns.en: their businesses, how they can enhance their customer experience, how they can create efficiency in their businesses. We've committed $500 million to that.
turns.zh: ——自己的生意里，怎么提升客户体验，怎么在自己业务里创造效率。我们已经为此承诺投入 5 亿美元。

turns.en: We're also making more capital available for small businesses in the program. Let me just ask a last question, David, which is obviously there's been a lot of concern and volatility in the market in the last couple of weeks around this AI theme.
turns.zh: 我们还为项目里的小企业投入了更多资金。最后一个问题，David——过去几周市场围绕 AI 这个主题出现了很多担忧和波动。

turns.en: Are you concerned at all about its durability and sustainability? With a long-term view, I'm not concerned about its durability and sustainability.
turns.zh: 它的持续性和可持续性，你担忧吗？从长期来看，我不担心它的持续性和可持续性。

turns.en: I think this is going to be a very important technology that is going to be deployed in an enormous application layer in businesses and enterprise and government in a whole variety of ways, but it's going to take 10, 20, 30 years for us to really appreciate the impact of all this.
turns.zh: 我认为这将是一项极其重要的技术，会在商业、企业和政府的庞大应用层里以各种各样的方式被部署；但要让我们真正领会它全部的影响，还需要 10 年、20 年、30 年。

turns.en: In the meantime, there's more demand for compute right now than there is compute, and there's an expectation of a very significant build-out, whether or not the build-out is going to be as significant as some people are saying, whether we're going to spend $5 trillion on the build-out or $10 trillion on the build-out, or more, I don't think anybody really knows.
turns.zh: 在此期间，眼下对算力的需求比现有的算力还多，而且人们预期会有非常大规模的基建扩张。至于这轮扩张到底会不会像有些人说的那样宏大——我们会为这轮扩张花上 5 万亿还是 10 万亿美元、甚至更多——我想没有人真正知道。

turns.en: It will be a journey. It won't be a straight line. There'll be accelerations and pullbacks, and so I think one of the things that's going on in the market that's creating a little bit of volatility is people really trying to understand what's the right way for this to develop, what will be the pace of the development, where are the best opportunities, a lot of capital flows.
turns.zh: 这将是一段旅程，不会是一条直线，会有加速也会有回撤。所以我觉得市场上正在发生、并制造了一点波动的东西之一，就是人们真的在试图理解：这项技术正确的演进方式是什么，发展速度会怎样，最好的机会在哪里，还有大量的资本流动。

turns.en: Certainly, as the cost of capital goes up, it changes people's views, and you have two dynamics there. One, a lot of capital creates competition for capital, cost goes up, two interest rates have gone up quite a bit this summer for other reasons, and those things push at some of these business models, and so this is going to be a journey, but I'm quite confident if you can look out in the medium or the longer term that the benefits from this are
turns.zh: 当然，随着资本成本上升，人们的看法会改变，这里面有两股动力。一是大量资本造成对资本的竞争，于是成本上升；二是利率因为其他一些原因在这个夏天涨了不少——这两点都在挤压其中一些商业模式。所以这会是一段旅程，但我相当有信心，如果你把目光放到中期或更长期，从中获得的好处将会是了不起的。

turns.en: going to be terrific, but we'll probably have a recalibration here in the markets at some point in time. As people reevaluate how much demand for compute will there be, what will be the line of growth of that demand, what kind of infrastructure do we really need, how is new technology coming in that makes the chips faster, cheaper, so it changes our perspective on how much data center capacity is needed.
turns.zh: 不过市场在某个时点大概会经历一次重新校准。当人们重新评估对算力的需求会有多大、需求的增长曲线是怎样的、我们真正需要什么样的基础设施、什么样的新技术会让芯片更快更便宜——这些都会改变我们对到底需要多少数据中心容量的看法。

turns.en: Those are all reasonable questions and things that I think we'll learn a lot more about the coming years. Thanks so much for joining us, David, for your insights on this very important topic, and I look forward to our conversation early next year.
turns.zh: 这些都是合理的问题，我想在未来的几年里我们会对此了解更多。非常感谢你参加节目，David，感谢你在这个极其重要话题上的洞见，也期待我们明年年初的对话。

turns.en: Thanks so much. It's great to see you, Allison. Thank you. And thank you for listening to this episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges, which was recorded on Monday, October 26th.
turns.zh: 太感谢了。很高兴见到你，Allison。——也谢谢你。感谢收听本期 Goldman Sachs《Exchanges》，这期节目录制于 10 月 26 日，星期一。
